subject: dplyr package,  select() function, starts_with() argument

messages.author: 3ca90093cd180bb5
messages.subject: dplyr package,  select() function, starts_with() argument
parts:
Dear R users,

I want to select columns that start with "Initiator" OR with "Recipient" in a dataframe. How should I tell these information to the starts_with() agreement in select() function in dplyr package?

I tried using select(df, starts_with(c("Initiator", "Recipient"), ignore.case = FALSE)), and select(df, starts_with("Initiator" | "Recipient", ignore.case = FALSE)). Neither one works. 

All the examples that I am able to find are only with one string. Anyone has any idea?

Thanks,
Jane

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: dplyr package, select() function, starts_with() argument
parts:
I believe you're looking for:

select(df, matches("Initiator|Recipient"))


Note that we need to use 'matches' take advantage of 'regular
expression notation' such as the '|' operator. (You can modify the
regular expression to get the equivalent of "starts_with" if you need
to match a column that is really called something that only starts
with the term Initiator, etc)

messages.author: 2b27719db7267c87
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: dplyr package, select() function, starts_with() argument
parts:
An alternative way to do that selection is to index with grepl(), which returns a logical vector indicating whether each element matches the specified pattern.

df[grepl("^Initiator|^Recipient", names(df))]

Bonnie
